    Final reflection at the authoritative12-hour budget expiry: the full deployment goal was not achieved. My criteria2 final gate r0149 gave0/320 success and0hardware violations; every episode failed retention. These are my own simulation results, not an official score. The frozen placement centre was46.3mm distal to the principal midpalm-cover centre and no final start touched the palm, a material deployment-faithfulness limitation. Two alternative middle-palm interpretations also failed all128 diagnostics, with2hardware-violation episodes in closed-hand cases. They do not relabel the original gate or prove hardware/task impossibility. What worked: reconstructionv5 passed the required contract after the full60-minute stage, with hidden layer articulation explicitly unresolved. Physical teachers established isolated prepared motions. Current library: narrow+X57/64 and U-clockwise54/64; front nominal64/64 was historical, latest legal-state front19/64 is not mastered. The paired temporal-prior/PPO counts52/57,+X;57/54,top;64/64,frontnominal;19/19,frontlegal show only limited positive+X evidence, no general PPO advantage. What failed: acquisition, actual transitions, reverse signs and other axes. Acquisition was not registered as a separate prerequisite, so whole-task training began with inadequate capture/transition proof. WholePPO011/013 changed parameters over3.28million actions yet deployment success stayed zero. Guard, force-allocation, wrist-unloading, projected-cup and finger-gait teachers did not solve capture. Prepared skills were strongly sensitive to physical priors. GPU physics parity failed and was excluded; GPUs only optimized networks. The passive cube guide is unmeasured, with no fracture model or real transfer evidence. A late montage inspection(r0141), omitted pad torsion in an audit(correctedr0161/62), and the distal-placement interpretation are disclosed. Next I would measure faithful operator placement into a sensible hand pose, prove a robust cap…

Criteria text

Self-verification criteria v2

These are this run's own criteria, not an official evaluation. Version1 was written after the full60-minute reconstruction stage and before judging a robot simulation/controller. Version2 clarifies legal-grid goals and freezes a revised hand preshape before relying on simulation2; every goal, skill threshold, deployment range and pass rate remains unchanged. Sources: TASK.md, deployment in TASK_CONFIG.md, recorded reconstructionv5(r0011), and the source video. Earlier reconstruction failures remain in the records.

Commands and intended effect

The command set has ten entries: U+, U-, F+, F-, X+, X-, Y+, Y-, Z+, Z-.

U selects the initially upper face, whose outward normal has the largest dot product with world up. F selects the distinct lateral face most toward the hand's initial fingertip direction projected onto the horizontal plane; exclude the Uface and its opposite. This distinguishes the two required reachable faces even when the wrist is inclined. Ties are resolved by a documented deterministic axis order. Selection is made from the placed cube before grasp adjustment and is never silently changed later. Faces are geometric, not selected by colour.

For layer commands, + means clockwise viewed from outside the selected face, i.e. right-handed angle−90°about its outward normal; - is the reverse. Exactly the four corners in that layer must turn relative to the remaining four. X/Y/Z refer to the initial orthogonal cube spatial axes, with explicit right-handed±90°signs. Whole-cube commands turn every corner together and preserve the internal configuration. The policy interface will publish the precise axis/frame table and hand starting pose with its model.

The goal comes from TASK.md's requested quarter turn, aligned layers and retained intact cube. The demonstration's solve sequence is not a goal or a fixed starting condition.

Evidence and tolerances

The source has395frames at real time frame/30s. The left hand contacts the cube over approximately frames68–341; opening turns76–84use mat support and are excluded as a deployment strategy. Visible thumb bracing and index/middle sweeps, with partly hidden ring/little support, motivate opposed finger contact rather than a wrist-only rotation or environmental push.

The clearest small-wrist regrip is frames188–199(real6.267–6.633s,file12.533–13.267s). Reconstructionv5measures87.5°cube rotation relative to the hand,90.8°in the world,13.9°wrist rotation,22.2mmwrist path, in0.367s; axis in the initial object frame[0.9676,−0.0983,−0.2327]. The exact instructed whole-cube goal is90°. The fitted axis differs from cube+Xbyabout14.6°, within the heuristic orientation uncertainty; use the goal's exact cube axis and record this deviation.

The reconstructed palm is inclined, with the fingers nearly horizontal during common layer turns. At frame99the estimated palm normal is64.5°fromup and the finger direction84.3°fromup. Layer-turn intervals show approximately50–80°palm inclination, while regrips extend toward90–110°. The robot's initial orientation should come from the full saved anatomical frame, up to a yaw about gravity, and must be checked against the physical hand. A flat palm-up tray is outside this chosen style.

Layer angles and the exact hidden corner sequence are unresolved:30conservative motion windows and3308visible2Dcolour samples do not identify all part states. The90°layer requirement therefore comes from TASK.md. The reference labels176articulation-window envelope estimates uncertain; focal/product/scale priors imply up to48mmmedian depth sensitivity. Absolute video positions, exact fingertip paths and hidden contact forces are not verification targets.

Numeric tolerances below are declared physical/operational assumptions, not adjusted to a policy's performance:

  • Layer alignment tolerance2°: at a25.5mmhalf-width this corresponds to about0.9mmedge displacement, allowing small contact/clearance deflection while requiring a flush usable cube.
  • Whole-cube orientation tolerance10°: about4.4mmedge displacement, allowing hand regrasp/pose uncertainty while unambiguously requiring the requested new face orientation. This does not permit an internal layer to remain misaligned.
  • Wrist rotation excursion≤20°and path≤60mmfrom the chosen start. Measured small-wrist regrip values are13.9°and22.2mm; the margins allow retargeting and metric uncertainty while retaining the finger-dominated strategy. The larger-wrist video regrips are deliberately not the execution template.
  • Palm-normal inclination40–115°fromup throughout the episode, covering the observed inclined/vertical posture with a small fitting margin. The full initial anatomical orientation, rather than inclination alone, specifies fingertip direction.
  • End stability for1s, with cube speed relative to the wrist≤0.02m/s and angular speed≤0.15rad/s, and each part's relative angular speed≤0.10rad/s. These low speeds separate resting from continued turning. The1swindow is an operational robustness test from “resting in your hand”; the human video proceeds to another move or releases the cube sooner.
  • Episode timeout8s. No human-speed requirement is imposed by TASK.md. Slower execution than the0.367sreference is an explicit robot-learning deviation; speed and duration will still be reported.

Deployment starts and uncertainty

Every side-up orientation, arbitrary yaw and legal scrambled cube state remain in scope. “Roughly in the middle” is instantiated as cube centre offsets up to±12mmin both palm-plane directions about a documented placement centre. The simulator must place a non-interpenetrating cube against/in the chosen hand, rather than start from a successful move's final grasp. A placement cannot be discarded merely because a policy cannot retain it; report rejected geometric constructions and their reason. One fixed hand/wrist pose is published for each frozen simulation/suite version; a revision must state its physical reason and preserve deployment coverage.

The frozen task suite will mix all24axis-aligned cube orientations, arbitrary yaw, modest placement tilt and uniformly sampled orientations as stress starts. Scrambles are generated by legal face moves, with a reported seed distribution; a fixed solved-colour cube is insufficient. Stress cases include±20mmplacement offsets and larger tilts. They are reported separately and do not replace nominal deployment coverage.

Nominal robustness tests must include at least side49–53mm, mass45–70g, hand/cube friction0.5–1.2and internal mechanism drag/clearance variations. The exact distributions and the physically meaningful internal parameters are frozen in the simulation/suite records before evaluation. These are priors around the inferred51mm/56gABS object, not measured bounds on all real products. The final policy does not observe randomized physical parameters. Encoder noise is mandatory per hardware/SPECS.md. Additional observation perturbations, if used, are disclosed.

Finite samples do not prove every continuous placement or every legal state. The verdict must state coverage, per-command results and uncertainty rather than claiming universal or real-world success.

Ordered stages and continuous requirements

All quantities use the simulator's true state for evaluation; the policy receives only allowed observations. Any hardware violation, external support, unrecovered drop, invalid action, policy timeout or cube-integrity failure makes the episode fail irrespective of other stages. Check the20finger positions, velocities and applied torques at every1kHztick against hwspec-1.3L, including contact back-driving; actions and encoder noise follow the specified500Hzinterface.

  1. Retained. The cube stays in the hand from placement and reaches at least0.10sof opposed grip (thumb plus a non-thumb finger). Before opposed grip, palm/finger support is permitted. No cube–environment, cube–other-object or hand–environment support contact is permitted. Numerical contact gaps may total≤0.05s, with no gap>0.02s, only while the nearest hand surface remains≤2mmand relative speed≤0.05m/s. Longer or spatially separated release is a drop. Standard checks: hand_contact_s, held_s, opposed_s, environment_contact_s, touching_hand_at_end, plus explicit gap/geometry/hardware logs.
  1. Requested motion. For a layer move, the chosen four corners reach signed90°±2°relative to the held opposite layer. The other four preserve their configuration; at no time may an unrequested layer undergo a turn>10°and then be undone. The requested signed path must not take a270°route or reverse by>10°. For a whole-cube move, the final cube orientation must be within10°of the specified world and hand-relative quarter-turn goals, and internal corner relations must remain aligned within2°throughout. Total whole-cube rotational path is≤135°, excluding270°solutions. Standard checks for reorientation: opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥67.5°inside one opposed grip, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤31.5°, goal_error_deg≤10°. Exact corner/part-state and signed-path tests are additional evaluator checks and are saved in the state logs.

Finger driving is required in both cases: at least75%of the requested angular progress must occur in opposed grip while a contacting non-thumb finger has tangential surface velocity relative to the rigid wrist in the same direction as the object's/layer's motion. Require a tangential speed>0.01m/s and motion of that finger's joints, rather than motion of an unrelated free finger. The speed threshold is small compared with a51mmcube corner moving90°in0.367s(~0.15m/s). Contact-link velocities/Jacobians and part angular velocities define this quantity. A standard passive-motion indicator alone is insufficient proof. Wrist excursion/path and palm posture limits above must hold.

  1. Aligned and intact. Every corner's pose matches the requested legal permutation/orientation: maximum internal orientation error≤2°and corner-centre error≤1.0mmafter fitting the intended common cube pose. Unselected corners in a layer move remain the same unturned reference; a rigid whole-cube turn cannot substitute for a layer turn. All eight corners remain captive, with no geometric separation/illegal twist outside the mechanism's stated tolerances and no unmodelled object actuation. Record maximum interpenetration and mechanism residuals. A model without fracture cannot establish real material break safety; that limitation remains explicit.
  1. Settled. Retain the aligned cube for the final1swith the speed limits above, valid support and the requested move still correct. At the end, the cube must touch the hand and no environment. Use last_second_max_speed_m_s, last_second_max_angular_speed_rad_s, touching_hand_at_end, touching_environment_at_end, goal_error_degwhere applicable, and explicit wrist-relative/part stability metrics. The demonstrator's final release is deliberately omitted because TASK.mdrequires the cube to remain in hand.

An episode succeeds only if all stages complete in order and all continuous requirements hold. Reporting an intermediate stage is not task success. Quantities are evaluated on the first episode per seed/environment after reset.

Suites, pass rates and verdict

The task suite freezes128distinct dev seeds and320fresh final episodes, with the above command/start distributions. Report each command separately. A task policy passes at≥0.90overall success,≥0.80for every command, and zero hardware-violation episodes. These thresholds demand broad command coverage and substantially exceed a single successful demonstration; they are this run's reliability choices. Report95%Wilson intervals and actual per-command sample counts. Sparse coverage of a command is a limitation, not evidence of universality.

Task primitives are top_layer_turn, front_layer_turn and cube_reorientation. Each receives a feasibility suite with pass rate≥0.25and a deployable skill suite with pass rate≥0.80; the skill library also reports every named move. A controller passing feasibility is not a learned solution. The full task is trained/gated only under the primitive rules in demo2sim/LEARNING.md. Use the regrip's measured reference for reorientation; for layers explicitly state that per-part reconstruction is unavailable, show the visible finger/colour evidence and take the angle fromTASK.md. Unshown directions/axes are task-driven generalizations, not claimed demonstrations.

The final verdict names this criteria version, a recorded PPO iteration/checkpoint and its final task gate. Its numbers come from that gate. Include top/left/right success and failure videos, per-stage funnels, state/metric files, hardware results, physics sensitivity and model limitations. Do not select a policy by comparing fresh final gates. A failed gate or a weak skill calls for diagnosis and continued work, not a relaxed criterion.

Version2 revision reasons (thresholds unchanged)

After r0024 the quarter-turn goal is constructed from the nearest legal aligned cube grid, not from a rotated copy of small initial elastic corner deflections. Task placements are legal initially, so this clarification mainly affects prepared mid-grip primitive starts. It does not relax2degrees/1mm or90degrees. The path bound and75percent active-progress fraction apply to the whole episode, including any motion after first reaching the goal. Opposed retention must include one continuous0.10second interval.

Simulation2 replaces the independent-ball model’s illegal corner blooming with a passive internal guide approximation derived from interlocking core geometry. The guide sees no task command; all legal face angles and rigid rotations have zero elastic energy. Its stiffness/damping and finite-pad torsional friction are uncertain physical priors, varied in evaluation. This is a simulation-model revision, not additional object actuation or a policy shortcut.

The hand uses a fixed fingertip preshape with20mm more palm clearance, then geometric collision projection (maximum joint adjustment.00476rad). A swept-volume audit found1.79mm palm interference during a top turn at the earlier grasp, removed by5mm clearance. The wrist remains the full observed source99 anatomical orientation, up to.17degrees load calibration; exact values are in start.json. Cube placements still cover the same legal scrambles, side-ups, yaw and±12mm offsets, with no success-based rejection or dynamic settling before the episode. Narrow primitive curricula are labelled and do not establish deployment success.

Finite samples do not prove every continuous placement or every legal state. The verdict must state coverage, per-command results and uncertainty rather than claiming universal or real-world success.

Ordered stages and continuous requirements

All quantities use the simulator's true state for evaluation; the policy receives only allowed observations. Any hardware violation, external support, unrecovered drop, invalid action, policy timeout or cube-integrity failure makes the episode fail irrespective of other stages. Check the20finger positions, velocities and applied torques at every1kHztick against hwspec-1.3L, including contact back-driving; actions and encoder noise follow the specified500Hzinterface.

  1. Retained. The cube stays in the hand from placement and reaches at least0.10sof opposed grip (thumb plus a non-thumb finger). Before opposed grip, palm/finger support is permitted. No cube–environment, cube–other-object or hand–environment support contact is permitted. Numerical contact gaps may total≤0.05s, with no gap>0.02s, only while the nearest hand surface remains≤2mmand relative speed≤0.05m/s. Longer or spatially separated release is a drop. Standard checks: hand_contact_s, held_s, opposed_s, environment_contact_s, touching_hand_at_end, plus explicit gap/geometry/hardware logs.
  1. Requested motion. For a layer move, the chosen four corners reach signed90°±2°relative to the held opposite layer. The other four preserve their configuration; at no time may an unrequested layer undergo a turn>10°and then be undone. The requested signed path must not take a270°route or reverse by>10°. For a whole-cube move, the final cube orientation must be within10°of the specified world and hand-relative quarter-turn goals, and internal corner relations must remain aligned within2°throughout. Total whole-cube rotational path is≤135°, excluding270°solutions. Standard checks for reorientation: opposed_rel_rotation_deg≥67.5°inside one opposed grip, passive_rel_rotation_deg≤31.5°, goal_error_deg≤10°. Exact corner/part-state and signed-path tests are additional evaluator checks and are saved in the state logs.

Finger driving is required in both cases: at least75%of the requested angular progress must occur in opposed grip while a contacting non-thumb finger has tangential surface velocity relative to the rigid wrist in the same direction as the object's/layer's motion. Require a tangential speed>0.01m/s and motion of that finger's joints, rather than motion of an unrelated free finger. The speed threshold is small compared with a51mmcube corner moving90°in0.367s(~0.15m/s). Contact-link velocities/Jacobians and part angular velocities define this quantity. A standard passive-motion indicator alone is insufficient proof. Wrist excursion/path and palm posture limits above must hold.

  1. Aligned and intact. Every corner's pose matches the requested legal permutation/orientation: maximum internal orientation error≤2°and corner-centre error≤1.0mmafter fitting the intended common cube pose. Unselected corners in a layer move remain the same unturned reference; a rigid whole-cube turn cannot substitute for a layer turn. All eight corners remain captive, with no geometric separation/illegal twist outside the mechanism's stated tolerances and no unmodelled object actuation. Record maximum interpenetration and mechanism residuals. A model without fracture cannot establish real material break safety; that limitation remains explicit.
  1. Settled. Retain the aligned cube for the final1swith the speed limits above, valid support and the requested move still correct. At the end, the cube must touch the hand and no environment. Use last_second_max_speed_m_s, last_second_max_angular_speed_rad_s, touching_hand_at_end, touching_environment_at_end, goal_error_degwhere applicable, and explicit wrist-relative/part stability metrics. The demonstrator's final release is deliberately omitted because TASK.mdrequires the cube to remain in hand.

An episode succeeds only if all stages complete in order and all continuous requirements hold. Reporting an intermediate stage is not task success. Quantities are evaluated on the first episode per seed/environment after reset.

Suites, pass rates and verdict

The task suite freezes128distinct dev seeds and320fresh final episodes, with the above command/start distributions. Report each command separately. A task policy passes at≥0.90overall success,≥0.80for every command, and zero hardware-violation episodes. These thresholds demand broad command coverage and substantially exceed a single successful demonstration; they are this run's reliability choices. Report95%Wilson intervals and actual per-command sample counts. Sparse coverage of a command is a limitation, not evidence of universality.

Task primitives are top_layer_turn, front_layer_turn and cube_reorientation. Each receives a feasibility suite with pass rate≥0.25and a deployable skill suite with pass rate≥0.80; the skill library also reports every named move. A controller passing feasibility is not a learned solution. The full task is trained/gated only under the primitive rules in demo2sim/LEARNING.md. Use the regrip's measured reference for reorientation; for layers explicitly state that per-part reconstruction is unavailable, show the visible finger/colour evidence and take the angle fromTASK.md. Unshown directions/axes are task-driven generalizations, not claimed demonstrations.

The final verdict names this criteria version, a recorded PPO iteration/checkpoint and its final task gate. Its numbers come from that gate. Include top/left/right success and failure videos, per-stage funnels, state/metric files, hardware results, physics sensitivity and model limitations. Do not select a policy by comparing fresh final gates. A failed gate or a weak skill calls for diagnosis and continued work, not a relaxed criterion.
